Definition: properly, to be rubbed or worn; hence (figuratively) to be weak, sick, afflicted; or (causatively) to grieve, make sick; also to stroke (in flattering), entreat
BiblicalUsage: Chalah means to be weak, sick, worn — and, strangely, to entreat earnestly. Joseph was told his father was sick, Moses besought the LORD after the golden calf, the next generation would see the sicknesses of the land, and Samson said if they bound him with green withs he would be weak as any other man.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sickness and prayer share one root because they share one posture: worn down, and turning to God. Moses besought because Israel was sick, and Samson was weak because he had forgotten it.
RelatedPeople: Joseph, Son of Jacob; Moses; Samson
